title: 11th Word: Construction of the Palace and Appointment of the Explaining Master

questions.question: What project did the king begin in order to fulfill his purpose?
questions.answer: He began building an immense and magnificent palace.

questions.question: How was the palace made beautiful and impressive?
questions.answer: It was arranged into splendid sections, decorated with precious treasures, and adorned with skillful artistic work and wise design.

questions.question: What did the king prepare inside the palace after finishing its construction?
questions.answer: He prepared generous dining tables filled with many kinds of food and blessings for different groups.

questions.question: Why did the king invite people from all parts of his land?
questions.answer: He wanted them to enjoy the feast and look at the display in the palace.

questions.question: Whom did the king appoint after inviting the people?
questions.answer: He appointed a highest-ranking commander to serve as a teacher and guide.

questions.question: What were some main duties of this teacher?
questions.answer: He was to explain the purpose of the palace, teach the meanings of what was inside it, describe its maker, and show people the proper way to respond.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the king’s visibility to the visitors?
questions.answer: The king himself was not seen directly by them.

questions.question: Why did the teacher have assistants in different parts of the palace?
questions.answer: They helped guide people throughout the various areas while he addressed them from the main hall.

questions.question: Where did the teacher stay while making his announcement?
questions.answer: He remained in the largest room among his students.

questions.question: How are wisdom and knowledge shown in the way the palace is described?
questions.answer: The palace is presented as carefully planned, artistically ordered, and full of meaningful details rather than random decoration.

questions.question: What relationship is shown between the banquet and the rest of the palace?
questions.answer: The food was part of the same display of generosity, beauty, and purposeful craftsmanship.

questions.question: What is the main setting described in the passage?
questions.answer: A grand palace built by a king for a meaningful public display.

questions.question: In what ways did the king use his own resources in the palace?
questions.answer: He used treasures, artistic skill, wisdom, and knowledge to shape and decorate it.

questions.question: What does the variety of food at the tables show about the king?
questions.answer: It shows his generosity, care, and ability to provide richly for many kinds of guests.

questions.question: Why was a separate table assigned to each group?
questions.answer: It shows that the arrangements were intentional and suited to the needs or place of each group.

questions.question: What was the teacher supposed to explain about the decorations and jewels?
questions.answer: He was to show what they pointed to about the owner’s excellence, skill, and perfection.

questions.question: Besides explaining the palace, what kind of behavior was the teacher meant to teach?
questions.answer: He was to teach the right manners and ceremonies for viewing and responding to what was there.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the statement that the king did not appear?
questions.answer: The visitors needed guidance to understand the king’s will and the meaning of the palace without seeing him directly.

questions.question: How does the passage connect beauty with meaning?
questions.answer: The beauty is not merely for pleasure; it serves as a sign that points to deeper realities about the maker.

questions.question: Why is the commander described as both a teacher and an instructor?
questions.answer: His role included both giving knowledge and training people how to act properly.

questions.question: What does the phrase about subtle arts and wise ordering suggest about the palace?
questions.answer: It suggests that everything in it was carefully measured, intentional, and full of refined craftsmanship.

questions.question: How does the passage present the palace as more than a building?
questions.answer: It presents it as a place of signs, lessons, hospitality, and guidance.

questions.question: What did the king do first in carrying out his purpose?
questions.answer: He had a huge and majestic palace built.

questions.question: Name two ways the palace was furnished or arranged.
questions.answer: It was divided into elegant living spaces and decorated with jewels and finely crafted works.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the banquet prepared in the palace?
questions.answer: It was extremely generous, beautiful, and filled with many kinds of excellent food.

questions.question: What was the teacher meant to make known to the people about the palace?
questions.answer: He was to make clear its purposes, inner meanings, and what its details revealed about its owner.

questions.question: What was the teacher supposed to explain about the works of art inside the palace?
questions.answer: He was to explain what they signified and how they reflected the owner’s perfections and skills.

questions.question: Why would visitors need someone to explain the palace to them?
questions.answer: Because its decorations and arrangements carried meanings that might not be understood on their own.

questions.question: What does the existence of assistants in each section tell us about the scale of the palace?
questions.answer: It suggests the palace was very large and needed organized guidance throughout.

questions.question: What kind of communication happened in the largest apartment?
questions.answer: The main teacher addressed all the onlookers from there.

questions.question: In this passage, how are knowledge and authority joined together?
questions.answer: The king appoints a high-ranking leader who has authority to teach the correct understanding and proper conduct.

questions.question: Why is it important that the teacher explains official ceremonies too?
questions.answer: Because understanding the palace is not enough by itself; people must also respond in the right way.

questions.question: What does the king’s construction of a vast palace show about his intention?
questions.answer: It shows that he intended to present something great, rich, and purposeful to his people.

questions.question: How were treasure and artistry brought together in the palace?
questions.answer: Precious materials from the treasury were combined with skilled craftsmanship and wise arrangement.

questions.question: Why is the food described in such a rich and detailed way?
questions.answer: To highlight the king’s generosity and to show that even the banquet was part of the larger display of excellence.

questions.question: Who was invited to the palace gathering?
questions.answer: The king’s people and subjects from across his lands were invited.

questions.question: What was the first broad responsibility given to the supreme commander?
questions.answer: He was to teach the purpose of the palace and the meanings of what it contained.

questions.question: What did the commander need to teach about the maker of the palace?
questions.answer: He needed to help people know the maker through the signs found in the palace and its contents.

questions.question: What does the passage indicate about the connection between the palace and its owner?
questions.answer: The palace reflects the owner’s qualities, so understanding it helps people understand him.

questions.question: Why were the palace’s decorations not enough by themselves?
questions.answer: Because without explanation, people might enjoy them but miss what they truly point to.

questions.question: What practical role did the assistants play?
questions.answer: They extended the teacher’s guidance throughout the palace’s many areas.

questions.question: Why is the commander’s final action in this passage significant?
questions.answer: His public announcement marks the beginning of direct guidance for the visitors.

questions.question: What kind of audience was the teacher addressing?
questions.answer: He was addressing spectators who had come to see and benefit from the palace.

questions.question: What did the king create before arranging the feast?
questions.answer: He first had a grand palace constructed and richly decorated.

questions.question: How does the passage show that the palace was carefully planned?
questions.answer: Its rooms were organized, its ornaments were deliberately chosen, and its furnishings were arranged with wisdom and skill.

questions.question: What does the mention of many forms of bounty add to the meaning of the scene?
questions.answer: It shows that the palace was a place of welcome, provision, and abundance, not only beauty.

questions.question: What does it mean that the banquet seemed to come through many refined arts?
questions.answer: It means the food was presented with such care and excellence that it reflected high artistry as well as generosity.

questions.question: Why was the supreme commander needed after the people arrived?
questions.answer: The visitors needed someone qualified to explain what they were seeing and how they should respond.

questions.question: What kinds of things inside the palace required interpretation?
questions.answer: Its ornaments, jewels, designs, and artistic details all needed explanation.

questions.question: What was the commander supposed to teach about conduct?
questions.answer: He was to teach the proper etiquette and ceremonial behavior desired by the king.

questions.question: How does the phrase about the king not appearing shape the teacher’s role?
questions.answer: It makes the teacher essential as the one who conveys the king’s intentions to the people.

questions.question: Why is the teacher’s place among his students meaningful?
questions.answer: It shows an ordered system of teaching, where he leads from the center while others assist him.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the visitors before the announcement was made?
questions.answer: They had access to the palace and its blessings, but they still needed guidance to grasp its true meaning.

questions.question: How does this passage connect enjoyment and responsibility?
questions.answer: People are invited to enjoy the gifts, but they are also expected to understand and respond rightly.

questions.question: What was the king’s main outward action in this passage?
questions.answer: He built and furnished an extraordinary palace for people to enter and observe.

questions.question: What features made the palace seem majestic?
questions.answer: Its great size, beautiful divisions, precious decorations, fine craftsmanship, and wise arrangement made it majestic.

questions.question: What was special about the food set out in the palace?
questions.answer: It was abundant, varied, carefully arranged, and assigned in a fitting way to different groups.

questions.question: What does the invitation to people from all regions suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the king intended a wide public witnessing of his generosity and display.

questions.question: What title or position was given to the one who would explain the palace?
questions.answer: He was appointed as the highest commander and served as the main teacher.

questions.question: What are three things the teacher had to clarify for the guests?
questions.answer: He had to clarify the palace’s purpose, the meaning of its contents, and the proper manners expected there.

questions.question: Why did the teacher need to describe both the palace and its maker?
questions.answer: Because the palace’s true significance lies in what it reveals about the one who made it.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about people left without such instruction?
questions.answer: They might see the outward beauty but fail to understand its message.

questions.question: How was teaching organized throughout the palace?
questions.answer: The main teacher stayed in the largest hall, and assistants were placed in each area.

questions.question: What was the function of the teacher’s announcement to the spectators?
questions.answer: It was to guide their understanding before they formed wrong conclusions about what they saw.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect pattern appears in the passage?
questions.answer: The king’s purposeful building leads to the need for explanation, which leads to the appointment of a teacher and assistants.

questions.question: Based on the whole passage, how should the palace be viewed?
questions.answer: It should be viewed as a meaningful display that points beyond itself and calls for informed understanding and proper response.
